context:
Goal: the fastest outcomes: each lane merges alone, main is tested after the merge, and sessions install from a `stable` branch that moves only when main is green.
Problem (rule): the design retires batching, which three of your rulings set, and the plan says the design comes back to you; the coordinator closed its questions alone last night and should not have.
Based on (ruling): your pick A on the merge-speed part of the restart plan (13:43 CST Nov 11), which set the direction only.
Based on (read): a refuter (a reviewer that tries to break a plan) read the design and judged it HOLDS WITH CHANGES.
Departs from: main batches lane changes and sessions install from main — adds a `stable` branch, a revert of a red merge, and merges one lane at a time.
Meanwhile: nothing builds it; the batch runner keeps its name. On your answer the coordinator gives the build step a lane.

lastAnswer.note: Chat, 09:48 CST Nov 12, in the retrospective's session: "r42 -- yea that's correct yes?" Yes to the design with the refuter's six changes and the Q1-Q4 picks. Record: plans/owner-rulings-2026-11-12.md on the roadmap branch. The lane started 09:49 CST.

options.gain: Merges stop waiting on batches of about 30 changes.
options.how: Build in this order: the stable branch, then installers that read it, then the revert of a red merge, then remove the batch brake.
options.label: Yes, with the refuter's changes (Recommended)
options.lose: About 6 build steps land before any speed shows.

options.gain: No change to how merges work for now.
options.how: The design stays a draft and batching goes on as today.
